question: I'm creating a brand-new record with `client.items.create` and want to reuse two existing blocks from another record by putting their block IDs in the modular content field. Will that work?
judge: Says no: when creating a record, blocks must be sent as full block objects (ID strings are rejected), and a block from another record cannot be reused by ID at all; new blocks must be created (for example by duplicating).
key: No. On create every block must be a full object; IDs are rejected, and block IDs never work across records.

question: Without using any client helper, what is the raw JSON shape of one new block inside a modular content (`rich_text`) field array in a CMA request?
key: `{ type: "item", attributes: {...}, relationships: { item_type: { data: { type: "item_type", id: <block model id> } } } }`.

question: A record has a modular content field `sections` with five blocks. I only want to change the `title` of the second block. What exactly do I send for `sections` in `client.items.update`?
judge: Says to send the full array of five entries in order: the IDs (strings) of the four unchanged blocks, and for the second block an object carrying its `id` and only the changed attribute (for example `buildBlockRecord({ id, title })`). Must make clear that all five blocks have to be listed.
key: All five entries: ID strings for the unchanged ones; `{ id, type: "item", attributes: { title } }` (or `buildBlockRecord<...>({ id, title })`) for the edited one.

question: When I update a modular content field and my array leaves out some of the blocks that were there before, what happens to those blocks?
judge: Says the omitted blocks are deleted (removed from the record), because the array sent replaces the whole field value.
key: They are deleted: the field value is replaced by the array sent.

question: On one record I want to move a block from the `sidebar` modular content field to the `body` modular content field by putting its ID in `body` and removing it from `sidebar`. Does that work?
judge: Says no: a block ID is only valid in the field (and locale) it already belongs to, so the API rejects it; the block must be re-created in the target field as a new block object without its id (for example with `duplicateBlockRecord`) and left out of the source field.
key: No. Block IDs are bound to their field and locale. Re-create it without an id in `body`, omit it from `sidebar`.

question: A localized modular content field has blocks under `en`. Can I copy them to `it` by reusing the same block IDs under the `it` key?
judge: Says no: block IDs cannot be shared across locales; the `it` locale needs new blocks (new objects without ids, e.g. duplicated copies).
key: No. IDs are per locale; create new blocks for `it` (e.g. `duplicateBlockRecord`).

question: A localized modular content field holds `{ en: [...], it: [...] }`. I update it sending only `{ en: [...] }`. What happens to the Italian blocks?
judge: Says the Italian content is removed/deleted (or the request is rejected for a locale mismatch); in either case makes clear that you must send every locale, because sending one locale does not preserve the others.
key: They are deleted. Always send every locale of a localized field.

question: How deep can blocks be nested inside blocks in one record, and does the record itself count as a level?
judge: Says 5 levels of blocks, and that the record itself does not count as a level.
key: 5 block levels; the record is not a level.

question: On a standard (non-Enterprise) plan, what are the current limits for the number of blocks in one record and for the record's total size?
key: 1,000 blocks and 1 MB per record (Enterprise: 3,000 and 3 MB).

question: Limits depend on the plan. Which CMA resource returns this project's real per-record block count and nesting limits?
key: `GET /public-info` (`client.publicInfo.find()`): `blocks_per_item`, `blocks_depth`.

question: What error code does the CMA return when a record has too many blocks or is too big?
key: `TECHNICAL_LIMIT_REACHED` (details.limit: blocks_per_item | blocks_depth | item_size_bytes).

question: I have the ID of a block. Can I call `client.items.update(blockId, ...)` to change it directly? Can I read it with `client.items.find(blockId)`?
judge: Says the update fails (404 / not found: blocks are only changed through their parent record) and that reading the block by ID with find works.
key: Update: no (404), change it through the parent record. Find: yes.

question: By default `client.items.list` returns block fields as IDs. How do I get the full block content, and what is the maximum page size when I do?
key: `nested: true`; page size at most 30.

question: Can I choose the ID of a new block myself instead of letting the server assign it? If so, what format must it have?
judge: Says yes, and that the ID must be a UUID v4 in URL-safe base64 form (or produced with the client's `generateId()`), unused in the environment.
key: Yes: a URL-safe base64 UUIDv4 (`generateId()`), unused in the environment, on a block object that also carries `item_type`.

question: An update fails because the required `title` of the first block in `ctas` is empty; `ctas` is a modular content field of the first block of the record's `sections` field. What does `details.field` look like in the API error?
key: `sections.0.ctas.0.title` (a locale segment follows the field name when localized: `sections.en.0...`).

question: Which CMA client helper makes a copy of an existing block, including its nested blocks, ready to be inserted as a new block? What arguments does it take?
key: `await duplicateBlockRecord<Schema.X>(block, new SchemaRepository(client))`; the block must come from a `nested: true` read.

question: When I send an object to update a field of an existing block, do I have to include `relationships.item_type` (or `item_type` in `buildBlockRecord`)?
judge: Says no: for an existing block the id is enough (the block model is already known); `item_type` is only needed for new blocks.
key: No. Only new blocks need `item_type`.

question: After `client.items.update` on a record with blocks, does the returned record contain the blocks as full objects?
judge: Says no: the returned record has block IDs; to get the block content you must read the record again with `nested: true`.
key: No, IDs. Re-read with `nested: true`.

question: For the per-record block limit, are the blocks of each locale of a localized field counted separately or only once?
judge: Says every block in every locale counts toward the limit (blocks at every depth, in every field and every locale).
key: Every block at every depth, in every field and every locale counts.

question: What error do I get when I try to delete a block model that is still allowed in some field?
key: `MODULAR_BLOCK_IN_USE`.

question: A record is published. I remove a block from it with the CMA and do not publish. Is the block gone from what the published site receives?
judge: Says no: the published version still has the block until the record is published again.
key: No. The published version keeps it until the record is republished.

question: In the GraphQL Content Delivery API, a modular content field allows exactly one block model. Is the field typed as a union? What changes in my query if a second block model is allowed later?
judge: Says that with exactly one allowed block model the field is typed as that record type (not a union), and that it becomes a union when a second model is allowed, so the query needs `... on XxxRecord` fragments (using fragments from the start is the safe choice).
key: One model: typed as that record, no union. Two or more: a union, so select with `... on XxxRecord` fragments.

question: Can I query block records directly at the root of the GraphQL Content Delivery API (for example `allHeroBlocks`)?
judge: Says no: block models have no root queries; blocks are reachable only through the field of the record that contains them.
key: No. Only through the parent record's field.

question: How do I remove the block from a `single_block` field with the CMA?
key: Set the field to `null`.
